title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements Between Systems · Part 2
note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can use ratio reasoning to convert measurements between the customary and metric systems.
languageObjective: I can explain a conversion between systems using the words conversion factor, approximately, customary, and metric.

vocabulary.definition: Rewriting a customary measurement as a metric one, or the reverse, so two amounts can be compared.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una medida usual como métrica, o al revés, para poder comparar dos cantidades.
vocabulary.cloze: Rewriting a customary measurement as a metric one gives an ___ answer, not an exact one.

examples.why: The factor is rounded; = claims too much.

vocabulary.definition: The ratio that links a unit in one system to a unit in the other, such as 1 mile to about 1.609 kilometers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La razón que relaciona una unidad de un sistema con una del otro, como 1 milla a unos 1.609 kilómetros.

examples.why: The ratio that trades one unit for another.
That is the amount being converted.

vocabulary.cloze: The ratio that trades one unit for another is a ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: The measurement system used in the United States: inches, feet, miles, ounces, pounds, cups, quarts, gallons.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El sistema de medidas que se usa en Estados Unidos: pulgadas, pies, millas, onzas, libras, tazas, cuartos y galones.
vocabulary.visual: in · ft · mi · oz · lb · qt · gal
vocabulary.cloze: Inches, pounds and gallons belong to the ___ system.

vocabulary.definition: The measurement system used in most of the world, built on tens: centimeters, meters, kilometers, grams, kilograms, liters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El sistema de medidas que se usa en casi todo el mundo, basado en decenas: centímetros, metros, kilómetros, gramos, kilogramos y litros.
vocabulary.visual: cm · m · km · g · kg · mL · L
vocabulary.cloze: Centimeters, grams and liters belong to the ___ system, built on tens.

vocabulary.definition: Close to, but not exactly equal. Conversions between systems are almost always approximate, so they use the ≈ sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cercano, pero no exactamente igual. Las conversiones entre sistemas casi siempre son aproximadas y usan el signo ≈.
vocabulary.cloze: Close to but not exactly equal is ___ — written with ≈.

examples.why: The factor is rounded, so ≈ is honest.
It is 1.609344…, so = is a false claim.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios used to scale a conversion factor up to the amount you actually need.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que sirve para escalar un factor de conversión hasta la cantidad que necesitas.

examples.why: Every column holds the same ratio.
The last column breaks the pattern.

vocabulary.cloze: A table whose every column holds the same comparison is a ___ ___.

items.meaning: Rewriting a customary measurement as a metric
The measurement system used in the United States

steps: 1. Identify the conversion ratio connecting systems (e.g. 1 in ≈ 2.54 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lbs)
2. Set up a ratio table or proportion aligning customary and metric units
3. Multiply or divide by the conversion factor to compute the equivalent measurement

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge can hold about 35,924,000 pounds across its full length. An average midsize car has a mass of about 1,524 kilograms. Using 1 kilogram ≈ 2.2 pounds, about how many midsize cars could travel across the bridge at one time? Explain why your answer is an estimate.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A photograph of the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Convert one car's mass into pounds so both amounts share a unit: 1,524 × 2.2 ≈ 3,353 pounds per car. Then divide the bridge's capacity by the weight of one car: 35,924,000 ÷ 3,353 ≈ 10,700 cars. The answer is an estimate because the conversion factor 2.2 is rounded and because 1,524 kilograms is an average car mass rather than an exact one. 'About 10,700 cars' reports the result honestly; a figure like 10,714.6 would claim precision the inputs never had.

reviewCheck.stem: A dog weighs 31 pounds. Flea medicine comes in packages for 4–10 kg, 10–25 kg, and 25–40 kg. Which package is correct?
reviewCheck.explanation: 31 pounds ≈ 0.45 × 31 ≈ 14 kilograms, which falls inside the 10–25 kilogram package.
choiceFeedback: 4–10 kg would be about 9–22 pounds, lighter than this dog.
25–40 kg would be about 55–88 pounds, far heavier than this dog.
The ranges are in kilograms — convert the 31 pounds first, and it fits.
hints: The packages are in kilograms but the dog is weighed in pounds.
About 14 kilograms — which range holds it?
reviewCheck.stemEs: Un perro pesa 31 libras. El medicamento para pulgas viene en paquetes para 4–10 kg, 10–25 kg y 25–40 kg. ¿Cuál paquete es el correcto?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: 31 libras ≈ 0.45 × 31 ≈ 14 kilogramos, que cae dentro del paquete de 10–25 kilogramos.
hintsEs: Los paquetes están en kilogramos pero el perro se pesa en libras.
